title: Region declaration verification workshop notes
content:
Workshop objective:
- Create a lightweight, repeatable process for verifying customer-declared data residency ("region declaration") during onboarding and after configuration changes. Goal: make verification ~10–30m manual operator work + automated telemetry checks.

Attendees:
- Priya Shah (host)
- Marcus Lee (ops)
- Ana Gómez (legal & compliance)
- Ben Carter (SRE/runtime)
- Sanaa Ibrahim (solutions eng)

Context / why this matters (notes to self):
- Customers sign region commitments in contract; auditors may request evidence.
- We currently have ad-hoc verification per account — inconsistent.
- Need consistent artifacts we can attach to customer audit bundles.

Assumptions:
- Customer has either: hosted + region pin, dedicated pool with region tag, or private deployment with explicit region config.
- We can collect runtime telemetry (routing logs, instance region metadata, KMS key location) for the last 30 days.
- Legal will accept a curated bundle: timestamps + signed operator checklist + config snapshots.

Proposed verification checklist (operator + automated):
1) Contract mapping:
   - Confirm contract clause id and declared region(s) (from CRM).
   - Verify customer account id and tenant mapping in billing system.
2) Config snapshot (automated if possible):
   - Export tenant config: region pin, preferred zones, routing policy, pin timestamps.
   - Record model variants and fallback tiers (important for cross-region fallthrough).
3) Infrastructure evidence:
   - VM / container metadata showing region/zone tag for all active serving hosts in past 30 days.
   - IP egress samples and public prefixes to confirm no unexpected egress to disallowed territories.
   - KMS/HSM key metadata: region of key and key rotation log.
4) Routing & telemetry logs:
   - Sample request traces (x-request-id) showing routing decisions mapped to region attribute.
   - Gateway/router logs that indicate which pool served the request.
   - If cached KV prefix used, show cache hit locations and cache-eviction evidence.
5) Audit trail artifacts:
   - Operator-signed checklist with timestamp + operator id.
   - Snapshot of customer communication confirming region selection.
   - If fallback occurred during time window, include incident notes and justification (e.g., capacity failover).
6) Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
   - All serving nodes for sampled requests were in declared region or in approved fallback tier.
   - No evidence of persistent egress outside allowed geographies.
   - KMS keys are located in the declared region(s) when required by contract.

Minimum evidence bundle for customer/audit:
- Single ZIP with:
  - config_snapshot.json (tenant config)
  - route_trace_samples.log (5–10 traces spanning 7 days)
  - host_metadata.csv (host_id, region, start/end timestamps)
  - kms_keys.csv (key_id, region, created_at)
  - operator_checklist.pdf (signed, timestamped)
  - comms-thread.pdf (customer opt-in / confirmation)

Operator runbook (quick steps):
1) Pull tenant config by tenant-id (tool: tenantctl export --id).
2) Run automated verifier script: scripts/region_verif/collect_bundle.sh --tenant <id> --window 7d
3) Manually review traces with help from SRE if any trace hits non-declared region.
4) If discrepancy, escalate to oncall-residency (rotation roster in PagerDuty) and open PD-xxxxx.
5) Package zip, upload to secure audit bucket, attach to customer CRM record, notify legal.

Sample operator checklist items (for signing):
- "I confirm that the sampled serving hosts for tenant X were located only in <declared-region> during the sample window."
- "I confirm no unapproved egress to <excluded-regions> was observed in telemetry."
- "I confirm KMS keys in use are located in <declared-region>."

Customer-facing wording (snippet for emails or portal):
- "We have verified that your tenant's inference traffic was served from the selected region(s) during the verification period. Attached is the evidence bundle suitable for audit review. If you need a different window or additional detail, reply and we will extend the sample."

Open questions / unresolved decisions (workshop outcomes):
- Q1: Window length default (7d vs 30d). Ops preference = 7d for speed; Legal wants 30d for stronger evidence. Action: propose 7d default with optional 30d extended bundle. Owner: Ana. Target: 2024-09-05.
- Q2: How to represent approved fallback tiers in contract templates? Should fallback be allowed by default? Action: legal + product to draft fallback annex. Owner: Ana + Priya.
- Q3: Should automation redact IP addresses in bundles? Ops prefers non-redacted for internal debugging; legal prefers redacted for customer-facing deliverable. Action: add redaction toggle in collection script. Owner: Ben.
- Q4: Retention policy for evidence bundles (where to store and for how long). Action: SOC + Compliance to propose retention matrix. Owner: Marcus.

Action items (short):
- Ben: build collect_bundle.sh redaction flag + integration test. (jira:PD-4189)
- Priya: add operator checklist template to secure-templates repo. (github:repo/region-verif-templates#1)
- Ana: draft fallback annex language and get legal sign-off. (confluence:LEGAL-ANNEX-FALLBACK)
- Marcus: propose storage/retention paths and costs for audit bundles.

Notes to self / workshop tone:
- Keep this as lightweight as possible — primary value is repeatability and defensibility, not exhaustive forensics.
- Make operator checklist detachable (PDF) and machine-readable (small JSON) so we can attach to CRM and to S3 evidence bundles.
- Prioritize automation for steps 1–3; manual review only when traces show anomalies.

Appendix: quick command examples (ops cheat-sheet):
- tenantctl export --id T-12345 > config_snapshot.json
- scripts/region_verif/collect_bundle.sh --tenant T-12345 --window 7d --out /tmp/T-12345-bundle.zip
- python tools/trace_viewer.py --bundle /tmp/T-12345-bundle.zip --filter region!=eu-west1

Slack references from workshop: #private-deployments thread: "region-verif-aug21" (captures live decisions)

End of notes.

Document status: draft -> flagged for in_review; next meeting 2024-09-12 to close Q1/Q3.
summary: Workshop notes capturing a proposed operator-centric verification workflow for customer region declarations. Contains checklist, operator runbook, evidence bundle spec, sample comms, open questions, and action items.
